Record Class Placement

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.Placement
Record Components:
anchor - the anchor the panel is placed against, or null for the host's own reference
position - where, against it
public record Placement(@Nullable Anchor anchor, PanelPosition position) extends Record
Where a panel goes in one mode (7.4.0): what it is placed against, and its position there. A panel declares one for each ModeScope it shows in, with Panel.Builder.in(ModeScope, Placement), and the two modes' placements can be entirely different: a screen region in survival and beside an anchor in creative, say.
  • screen(PanelPosition): against the host's own reference, as every position(...) was before: the menu frame on a container screen, the screen on any other, the game window or the hotbar on the HUD, a standalone screen's main panel.
  • around(Anchor, PanelPosition): in the regions around an Anchor's box, stacking with the anchor's other panels: what an AnchorPanelAdapter did with on(anchor).
  • at(Anchor, int, int): at the anchor's box's top-left plus an offset, at the panel's natural size. No stacking, no room budget, and nothing keeps it on the screen: two panels at one spot overlap, and one past the edge is cut.
A placement with an anchor shows wherever that anchor's box is on the open screen: the box is its presence. An anchor with no box this frame (its thing not on this menu) leaves the panel out, and it claims nothing.

Placements are values: two built the same way are equal.
